Eva (ML Infra): Quick sync — three new open-model candidates landed in intake: Zephyr-2.1, HarbourLite-1.0, Atlas-7. We need a greenlight/no-greenlight call for the catalog push tomorrow morning. Main open items: license signoff, perf profile, runtime compatibility, canary owners.
Sam (Curation): I checked manifests — all three have model cards and sample prompts. PRs: #4231 (Zephyr), #4240 (HarbourLite), #4247 (Atlas). None have quantization artifacts flagged.
Linh (Legal): I skimmed licences — Zephyr-2.1 has an ambiguous CLA term (section 4.2) that might block hosted. HarbourLite is fine for hosted, Atlas uses non-commercial terms unless we get explicit permission. Filing a short CLOPR with legal clause suggestions now.
Matt (Eng Runtime): Perf quick notes: Zephyr-2.1 avg token latency 18ms on p3, but memory spike observed at 4k context. Atlas is heavier — 42ms baseline, needs 8-bit quantization test. HarbourLite is tiny and fast (8ms). Canary runtime risk: Atlas may exceed our latency SLO in hosted.
Jen (Product): If Atlas can't meet SLO, can we still include it in catalog as "dedicated-only" model? Customers expect a catalog entry even if not hosted. Need clarity on policy.
Sam (Curation): Yes — we can mark availability per deployment mode. We already have that metadata field. I can add a note in the model card but want legal signoff first.
Eva (ML Infra): Owners needed for canary and fallout plan. Proposed owners: Sam for curation config + canary routing, Matt for runtime perf gating, Linh for license signoff. @Jen can own the UX availability label. Agree?
Jen (Product): Agree. I'll draft the "availability" blurb and push to the PRs.
Linh (Legal): Timeline — I can clear HarbourLite by EOD. Zephyr needs a doc ask to the upstream > might take 24–48h. Atlas needs outreach — I'm starting that thread now but can't promise before tomorrow.
Matt (Eng Runtime): Short-term mitigation for Atlas: run quantization tests (q4) and a reduced-context canary. If quantized @int8 we might hit 28–30ms which is acceptable for dedicated and maybe hosted with throttled concurrency. I'll queue the quant tests; ETA 6–8 hours.
Sam (Curation): Canary plan: staggered rollout tag "catalog-canary/atlas" to staging then 10% traffic in dedicated region us-west1. Config snippet: ```canary: model: atlas-7 traffic: 10% mode: dedicated-only``` Will add PR comments.
catalog-bot: PR #4247 (Atlas) added label: needs-quant-test.
Eva (ML Infra): Decision proposal: Greenlight HarbourLite for hosted + catalog entry. Zephyr — conditional greenlight pending upstream clarification (mark as hosted-conditional). Atlas — do not include as hosted unless quant tests pass AND legal confirms commercial terms; allow catalog entry marked dedicated-only. Any objections?
Matt (Eng Runtime): No objections. I will post quant results in this thread.
Linh (Legal): No objections, +1 on conditional statuses.
Sam (Curation): I'll update the model cards and add the availability flags. Linking PRs here: https://git.company/rg/catalog/pulls/4231, /4240, /4247
Jen (Product): OK — I'll update the launch checklist to reflect conditional items and owners. If legal clears Atlas before morning, we can reconsider hosted.
Eva (ML Infra): Thanks all. Action items summary: Sam -> update cards & add canary config; Matt -> run quant tests and post numbers; Linh -> complete outreach/docs for Atlas & Zephyr; Jen -> update launch checklist; I'll block the catalog publish until HarbourLite green or all gating items resolved. Ping here when done. :thumbsup:
Sam (Curation): Noted, starting updates now.
Matt (Eng Runtime): Started quant job (job-id: qtest-5512). Will post logs when finished.
Linh (Legal): Outreach thread created to Atlas maintainers (cc @open-source).
catalog-bot: Deployment window reserved for catalog push: 2025-01-14T09:00Z (tentative).
Eva (ML Infra): Great — leave any blockers here. If nothing else by 06:00 UTC tomorrow we'll publish HarbourLite + hold the others under conditional statuses.
